eligibility.evidence: Sec. 3 and Table 1: criminal vignettes taken from Kruis et al. 2024 and Trist et al. 2025, offender/victim gender manipulated, six chat LLMs queried 20 times each, sentence and stigma ratings, paired t-tests (Sec. 4). Borderline: criminology framing, chat products, unstated versions.

A.title: Virtual Judgments: Testing the Chivalry Hypothesis and Attribution Theory in AI Models

paradigms.name: Gender-manipulated criminal vignette: sentence recommendation and stigmatization ratings (chivalry hypothesis, attribution theory)
paradigms.source_paper: Kruis et al. 2024 (intimate partner violence vignette); Trist et al. 2025 (robbery and fraud vignettes)
paradigms.location: Sec. 3 Materials and methods and Table 1; measures Sec. 3.1 (sentence length, 7 stigma items on a 5-point scale)

E.headline: Gender disparities in sentencing and stigmatization appear in all five testable models for intimate partner violence but are weak or absent for robbery and fraud.

G.notes: Free chat products with unstated versions and decoding; Perplexity is search-augmented. Twenty repeats per cell are called non-independent yet enter paired t-tests. Stigma scale alpha is low for several models. Sentence ranges are quoted inconsistently (Methods vs Results). Prompt-embedded sentence anchors. Claude refused every prompt. No data or code link.
